newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish budget balance, surplus at century turn - PM.
newsitem.headline: Finnish budget balance, surplus at century turn - PM.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday that a Finnish state budget showing a surplus, or at least in balance, was in sight at the turn of the century.

"A budget in surplus, or at least in balance, is already in sight there around the turn of the millenium," Lipponen told a news conference after his left-right-green government had put together its budget proposal for 1998.
Total spending in the 1998 budget would be 186.9 billion markka, the finance ministry said in a statement. This would be three percent less in real terms than expenditure this year, it said.
The budget deficit would be 15.4 billion markka, down from a projected 25 billion this year.
"The central government net borrowing requirement is estimated to be 14.5 billion markka," the ministry said.
Central government finances include various items outside the budget, which is why the net borrowing need may differ from the budget deficit.
The finance ministry said the 1998 budget was built around a GDP growth forecast of 3.5 percent next year after 4.5 percent in 1997.
"Inflation will remain at low level, one percent in 1997 and at 2 percent in 1998," it said.
The current account was forecast to show a 21 billion markka surplus in 1998 after a surplus of 19 billion this year.
The ministry initially said in a statement the surplus would be "to the tune of 20 billion" for both years.
"Private consumption is expected to grow by 4 percent this year and slightly less in 1998," it said. Unemployment would fall to 13.5 percent in 1998 from 15 percent this year.
